scope: Curated educational ophthalmology, systemic-health context, oculomics and model methods; not comprehensive ophthalmology training

topics.title: Diabetic retinopathy: what the grade describes
facts: Diabetic retinopathy affects retinal blood vessels in people with diabetes. Early disease may have no noticeable symptoms.
Clinical assessment considers visible retinal findings. A five-class model output is a research prediction, not a comprehensive eye examination.

source.title: Diabetic retinopathy: what the grade describes

topics.boundary: The current grader predicts DR severity only; it does not establish diabetes or exclude other eye diseases.

topics.title: How diabetes affects retinal vessels
facts: Long-term high blood glucose can damage small retinal vessels, affecting blood flow and allowing fluid leakage or bleeding.
Advanced disease can involve fragile new vessels. Segmentation geometry alone does not establish these clinical findings.

source.title: How diabetes affects retinal vessels

topics.boundary: This image pipeline does not measure blood glucose, diabetes duration, or verified lesion counts.

topics.title: Retina, macula and optic nerve
facts: The retina is light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. The macula supports detailed central vision.
Diseases affecting the macula and diseases affecting the optic nerve are different clinical problems; a DR grade does not summarize them all.

source.title: Retina, macula and optic nerve

topics.boundary: A fundus photograph shows posterior-eye structures; it does not replace tests of visual function or the anterior eye.

topics.title: Macular edema and the limits of a DR grade
facts: Macular edema is swelling in the macular region. It can cause blurred or distorted vision.
Clinical assessment may require retinal imaging beyond a color photograph. A DR severity label alone does not establish edema.

source.title: Macular edema and the limits of a DR grade

topics.boundary: This system does not process OCT images or provide a validated macular-edema diagnosis.

topics.title: Glaucoma and optic nerve assessment
facts: Glaucoma is a group of diseases that damage the optic nerve. Evaluation includes an eye examination and visual-field testing.
Eye pressure and optic-disc appearance are relevant, but a cup-to-disc ratio alone is not a glaucoma diagnosis.

source.title: Glaucoma and optic nerve assessment

topics.boundary: The X4 cup/disc measurements are image-derived descriptors. This DR model does not measure eye pressure or diagnose glaucoma.

topics.title: Age-related macular degeneration
facts: AMD affects the macula and central vision. Dry and wet AMD have different disease mechanisms and clinical courses.
Wet AMD involves abnormal vessels; a generic weak evidence map cannot distinguish it reliably from other retinal conditions.

source.title: Age-related macular degeneration

topics.boundary: No validated AMD or drusen detector is configured in this system.

topics.title: Cataract and image clarity
facts: A cataract is a cloudy area in the lens and can cause blurred or hazy vision.
Image clarity can affect retinal analysis, but rejection by an image-quality model does not establish cataract.

source.title: Cataract and image clarity

topics.boundary: The quality model estimates whether a photograph is usable; it does not diagnose the reason for poor image quality.

topics.title: Dry eye is different from retinal disease
facts: Dry eye occurs when tear quantity or function is inadequate and can cause discomfort and blurred vision.
Tear-film assessment differs from retinal vessel analysis.

source.title: Dry eye is different from retinal disease

topics.boundary: A retinal photograph and X1–X4 features cannot diagnose dry eye.

topics.title: Refractive errors and blurred vision
facts: Refractive errors occur when light does not focus correctly on the retina. Types include myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism and presbyopia.
Blurred vision has several possible causes, so it cannot be assigned to DR from a symptom alone.

source.title: Refractive errors and blurred vision

topics.boundary: No refraction or visual-acuity measurement is available from this pipeline.

topics.title: Retinal vein occlusion
facts: Central retinal vein occlusion occurs when a clot blocks the main retinal vein. Clinical assessment uses an eye examination and imaging.
It is a distinct disease from diabetic retinopathy and can affect retinal circulation.

source.title: Retinal vein occlusion

topics.boundary: Vein geometry and proxy maps do not provide a validated vein-occlusion diagnosis.

topics.title: Retinal detachment and urgent symptoms
facts: Retinal detachment occurs when the retina separates from its normal position.
A sudden increase in floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow warrants immediate assessment by an eye doctor or emergency service.

source.title: Retinal detachment and urgent symptoms

topics.boundary: Do not wait for this research grader to evaluate sudden visual symptoms.

topics.title: Systemic diabetes, blood pressure and eye health
facts: Diabetic eye health is connected to systemic diabetes management. Blood glucose, blood pressure and cholesterol are relevant clinical factors.
Retinal measurements do not substitute for the corresponding laboratory tests, blood-pressure readings or clinical history.

source.title: Systemic diabetes, blood pressure and eye health

topics.boundary: This system has no measured HbA1c, blood pressure or cholesterol and cannot infer their values from its DR output.

topics.title: Oculomics: connecting eye images with systemic health
facts: Oculomics studies whether ocular measurements can inform understanding of systemic health. Retinal images have been investigated for cardiovascular risk-factor prediction.
These tasks require separately trained models and external validation. A research association does not turn a DR grader into a general systemic-disease test.

source.title: Oculomics: connecting eye images with systemic health

topics.boundary: This deployment has no validated heart, kidney or neurological disease prediction head. No individual systemic diagnosis or risk is produced.

topics.title: Retinal images and cardiovascular research
facts: Poplin and colleagues trained separate deep-learning models to study cardiovascular risk factors using fundus photographs.
The study shows research potential; it does not validate cardiovascular predictions from this different DR model.

source.title: Retinal images and cardiovascular research

topics.boundary: No individual heart-attack probability, cardiovascular diagnosis or blood-pressure estimate can be calculated from this report.

topics.title: What eye measurements cannot establish about kidney health
facts: Diabetes can affect more than one organ system, so eye findings should be interpreted alongside systemic clinical assessment.
A retinal DR grade is not a kidney-function measurement. This report has no creatinine, estimated filtration rate or urine albumin data.

source.title: What eye measurements cannot establish about kidney health

topics.boundary: No kidney-disease model or kidney laboratory results are configured. A kidney diagnosis cannot be supplied from these image features.

topics.title: Why vessel geometry can provide contextual information
facts: A longitudinal cohort investigated retinal tortuosity, branching, fractal dimension and caliber in relation to later DR outcomes.
The associations were measured in a particular cohort and do not provide an individual diagnostic cutoff for this AutoMorph report.

source.title: Why vessel geometry can provide contextual information

topics.boundary: Associations are not causal explanations for this image or calibrated individual progression risks.

topics.title: Fractal dimension: pattern complexity
facts: Fractal dimension describes how vessel-pattern detail changes with scale. It is a structural complexity descriptor.
Its value depends on segmentation, region and measurement method.

source.title: Fractal dimension: pattern complexity

topics.boundary: A larger value is not automatically healthier or more diseased; no validated normal range is supplied here.

topics.title: Tortuosity and curvature describe different aspects of bending
facts: Path-to-chord tortuosity and squared-curvature descriptors summarize different aspects of vessel bending.
Values depend on segmentation and the measurement definition; the two quantities are not interchangeable.

source.title: Tortuosity and curvature describe different aspects of bending

topics.boundary: A curvature value alone cannot establish DR severity, hypertension or vascular damage.

topics.title: Vessel density differs from skeleton occupancy
facts: X1 skeleton occupancy measures the fraction occupied by one-pixel vessel centerlines; X4 vessel density measures segmented vessel occupancy.
They use different representations, so their percentages need not agree.

source.title: Vessel density differs from skeleton occupancy

topics.boundary: Neither density measure alone establishes ischemia or verified capillary loss.

topics.title: Length and topology need coordinate-aware interpretation
facts: Skeleton edge length is reported in processed-image pixels. Endpoint and junction counts describe the computed skeleton.
Pixel junction counts are not verified anatomical bifurcation counts.

source.title: Length and topology need coordinate-aware interpretation

topics.boundary: Processed-pixel length is not a calibrated physical vessel length.

topics.title: Grad-CAM is model attribution
facts: Grad-CAM uses class-score gradients and convolutional activations to localize model-relevant image regions.
Here it attributes the frozen fusion model image branch while tabular inputs remain fixed. It is separate from the trained X2 proxy features.

source.title: Grad-CAM is model attribution

topics.boundary: A highlighted region is not a confirmed lesion or proof that a feature causes disease.

topics.title: A lesion-trained representation is not a lesion detector
facts: The configured Huang checkpoint is a lesion-contrastive image encoder. It produces a representation for grading.
A separate detector is required to return lesion boxes or counts. Embedding components do not have named-lesion semantics.

source.title: A lesion-trained representation is not a lesion detector

topics.boundary: No lesion boxes, lesion counts or verified lesion-negative result are available from X3.

topics.title: What the X2 proxy maps mean
facts: The frozen X2 stream contains weak image-derived proxy statistics, not validated lesion detections.
Channel names describe the intended evidence cue; a proxy value is not a lesion probability.

source.title: What the X2 proxy maps mean

topics.boundary: This is an implementation capability statement. Proxy values cannot prove that the named lesion is present or absent.

topics.title: How the four streams complement the image
facts: X1 describes vessel skeleton structure; X2 supplies weak evidence proxies; X3 supplies lesion-trained image representations; X4 supplies vascular biomarkers.
The frozen fusion grader combines these with a retinal photograph. Missing required streams lead to a no-grade result.

source.title: How the four streams complement the image

topics.boundary: Different input roles do not establish causal contributions or clinical findings.

topics.title: Retinal photography and kidney-disease research
facts: Sabanayagam and colleagues developed a separate retinal-photo deep-learning algorithm to study chronic kidney disease detection in community populations.
That study supports investigating retinal photography as an adjunctive screening signal; it does not validate kidney predictions from this DR grader.

source.title: Sabanayagam et al. (2020), retinal photographs and chronic kidney disease

topics.boundary: This report has no validated kidney prediction, laboratory confirmation or individual kidney-risk estimate.

topics.title: Retinal foundation models and task-specific adaptation
facts: RETFound learns retinal-image representations through self-supervised pretraining and is adapted to specific downstream tasks.
A reusable representation still needs task-specific labels, evaluation and validation; it does not automatically provide every ocular or systemic diagnosis.

source.title: Zhou et al. (2023), a foundation model for retinal-image disease detection

topics.boundary: The deployed grader has no validated neurological or all-disease diagnosis head. Educational context is not a patient-specific systemic diagnosis.
